fields.description: DriveMod Tugger is Cyngn’s autonomous integration of a Motrec MT-160 tow tractor. Current developer specifications describe the 12,000 lb towing configuration with a separately rated 500 lb deck load, 65 × 30 × 55 in dimensions and 1,250 ± 100 lb mass depending on options. Maximum travel is 4 mph autonomous or 6 mph manual; battery operation is up to twelve hours depending on load/speed/usage, with five-hour charging and an unspecified charge window. Current turning radius is 53 in, minimum aisle 59 in and maximum grade 2.5 percent. The October 2023 preview’s 6,000 lb/54 in figures predate a documented 2024 upgrade. 3D-LiDAR mapping, FMS dispatch, manual override and redundant stop functions support site-specific workflows. Auto-unhitch and LTE retain attachment/optional scope; no blanket whole-system certification or guaranteed ROI is established.

highlights: Autonomous tugger uses 3D LiDAR mapping without floor guide wires, tape or magnets
Cyngn Insight and an onboard touchscreen support route changes, dispatch and manual override
EasyLaunch rental combines the Motrec-based vehicle, autonomy, mapping, training and support
Current autonomous Motrec MT-160 specifications give 65 × 30 × 55 in outer dimensions and 1,250 ± 100 lb mass depending on options. The 18 × 30 in deck is a separate area, not the vehicle footprint.

Current towing capacity is 12,000 lb; maximum onboard deck load is separately 500 lb. Autonomous speed is up to 4 mph and manual speed up to 6 mph; these are distinct operating modes, not two conflicting autonomous ratings.

The listed battery is 12.4 kWh lithium-ion at 48 V. Battery operation is up to twelve hours and charging is listed as five hours. Speed, load weight and usage affect endurance; exact charge-state/test conditions are unspecified and no independent continuous-duty guarantee follows.

The current specification states a 53 in turning radius, 59 in minimum aisle and 2.5% maximum slope. Percent grade is not degrees; commissioned cart-train clearance and environmental limits still require deployment assessment.

October 2023 preview figures were 6,000 lb towing and 54 in turn radius. The September 2024 release explicitly describes the upgrade from 6,000 to 12,000 lb; historical figures are not silently merged with today’s configuration.

The sensor suite lists 360° 3D LiDAR, 2D safety LiDAR, an IMU and wheel encoders. Virtual Bumper, emergency stops, LEDs and audio cues are developer safety functions. The catalog’s B56.5-compliant wording is attached to Virtual Bumper, not independently verified certification of every complete vehicle, site or cart train; three-times-faster reaction is a supplier comparison.

The datasheet lists auto-unhitch and blue light as optional features, and LTE as optional alongside Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac). Route dispatch, manual takeover and automatic charge/home missions are software functions; EasyLaunch has no numeric public price or guaranteed deployment/ROI result. The catalog lists pneumatic tires while the linked datasheet says solid/non-marking; exact supplied tire configuration remains unresolved.

highlights: Cyngn develops DriveMod autonomy and integrates it with industrial vehicles. Current Motrec MT-160 tugger, BYD forklift and historical Columbia stockchaser retain separate hardware/role attribution; DriveMod software is not itself another whole robot.

Current Tugger specifications separate twelve-thousand-pound towing, five-hundred-pound deck load, autonomous/manual speeds and load-dependent endurance. Historical6,000 lb/54 in preview and documented 2024 upgrade are not one contradictory unchanged revision.

BYD forklift development, paid deployment and later industry deployment announcements retain their dates. Current catalog load narrative does not certify every chassis, mast, load-center or current order package; former product path now redirects to another resource.

Columbia Stockchaser is explicitly documented in historical fleet/showcase announcements. Its present case-study landing title and downloaded Tugger wording do not justify forced model aliasing. Anonymous mining-OEM development work identifies no additional named complete robot.

Redundant sensing, Virtual Bumper, emergency stops and status/audio signals are developer safety functions. Component compliance wording, three-times reaction claims and customer-specific productivity/ROI figures are not independent whole-system certification, universal injury prevention or proven market leadership.
